newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico pays tribute to retiring cenbank governor.
newsitem.headline: Mexico pays tribute to retiring cenbank governor.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz paid tribute Friday to the country's veteran central bank president Miguel Mancera, who is to retire at the end of 1997 after 15 years in the job.
Banco de Mexico rules state that governing board members must step down at 65, an age Mancera will reach in December of this year.
That will make this year's Mexican Banking Convention the last for Mancera, who has held the top job at Banco de Mexico continuously since December 1982.
"This is the last occasion that Miguel Mancera is with us in his role as governor of Banco de Mexico," Ortiz told delegates.
After pointing out that he had worked with Mancera for most of his professional career, first as an official at Banco de Mexico and later in the Finance Ministry, Ortiz said:
"I just want to highlight his congruence, his firmness, his intellectual honesty and his vocation for service," Ortiz said to applause.
No decision has yet been taken on who will succeed Mancera, but officials say the likely front-runners are current Banco de Mexico deputy governors Francisco Gil Diaz and Jose Sidaoui.
